steps.title: Understand the problem
steps.description: I define what we're solving, for whom and under which rules. In Colombia that includes local laws and payment methods: consumer protection, data privacy, DIAN e-invoicing, Wompi and Nequi.

steps.title: Plan in phases
steps.description: The agent proposes the architecture and scope. I prioritize by business value and decide what stays out of each phase.

steps.title: Build through conversation
steps.description: The agent writes the code. I review how it behaves and correct the rules that don't match how the business really works.

steps.title: Verify with evidence
steps.description: Type checks, end-to-end tests against the real system, database schema checks and cleanup of test data. Nothing is accepted because it "should work".

steps.title: Close the phase and audit
steps.description: Every phase ends with a commit that explains the why. Periodically, a full audit (and, when the risk justifies it, a second AI) reviews the work and sets the next roadmap.

mine: Define the product and the business rules.
Correct the design when it doesn't match how the business works.
Prioritize: which phase comes next and what stays out.
Require evidence: passing tests and clean test data.
Cross-check with another AI when the risk justifies it.
Make the decisions with consequences: credentials, personal data, payments and legal texts.
agent: Propose the architecture and write the code.
Write and run the tests, migrations and analyses.
Work around technical blockers in the environment.
Document: READMEs, architecture notes, commit messages and reports.
Flag security, data and compliance risks so I can decide.

decisions.decision: The kitchen dispatches dish by dish, not whole orders.
decisions.why: That's how a real kitchen works. The change reshaped the system's entire state model.

decisions.decision: Two waiters never serve the same table.
decisions.why: It prevents duplicate charges and confusion. The administrator can reassign the table if a waiter is absent.

decisions.decision: Customer complaints (PQRS) are answered by a legal team, not the administrator.
decisions.why: Colombian consumer law sets deadlines with legal consequences. The answer must come from someone with that judgment.

decisions.decision: Every sale stores the discount campaign it had.
decisions.why: So we can answer why a product sold for less during a given week.

decisions.decision: A customer who leaves without paying is an authorized loss, not a sale.
decisions.why: The register has to match reality: it's recorded with a supervisor PIN and no fake sales.

practices: Audit before building further, and fix in order of impact.
End-to-end tests against the real system, with their own data deleted at the end.
Test concurrency: two people doing the same thing at the same time.
Rehearse data migrations inside a transaction that gets rolled back.
Scan the full history for secrets before publishing a repository.
One commit per phase, with a message that explains the why.

constraints.problem: A corporate proxy that blocks binaries and CDNs.
constraints.solution: Database engines installed by hand and system certificates for HTTPS calls.

constraints.problem: No administrator rights on the machine.
constraints.solution: Portable Node.js and tools that need no installation.

constraints.problem: Payment webhooks can't reach a local machine.
constraints.solution: Querying the payments API directly, which also found a payment that had never been recorded.

tools: Claude Code (Claude Opus) in VS Code
